options_considered: NVD CVE API; CISA KEV; MITRE ATT&CK; OWASP Cheat Sheets; MITRE CWE; NIST SP 800 series
chosen: All six as evidence sources; four as retrieval text (NVD and KEV are structured tool responses)
why_chosen: CVE investigation needs authoritative facts (NVD/KEV), adversary behaviour (ATT&CK), weakness definitions (CWE), defensive guidance (OWASP/NIST). Retrieval must not duplicate structured lookups.
why_others_rejected: Using NVD/KEV feeds as retrieval documents would double-count the 500-2000 document gate and let retrieval 'win' by re-reading data the tools already return (scope D5).
evidence_metric: 6 sources; 1,834 valid retrieval docs; NVD/KEV used only through tools
risks_limitations: Corpus is English-only and US-guidance heavy; ATT&CK Enterprise only (no Mobile/ICS).

options_considered: requests; urllib; httpx; curl subprocess
chosen: httpx with streaming download, redirects, 180 s timeout
why_chosen: Already a project dependency, supports HTTP/2 and streaming, raises on non-2xx, and avoids loading whole PDFs into memory.
why_others_rejected: requests adds a dependency with no streaming advantage here; curl is platform-specific and harder to error-check; urllib lacks ergonomic timeout/redirect handling.
evidence_metric: 10 sources downloaded; largest files streamed in 64 KB chunks
risks_limitations: No retry/backoff wrapper; a transient 5xx needs a manual rerun.

options_considered: Query live APIs on every request; cache with short TTL; pinned local snapshot
chosen: Pinned local snapshot with version metadata and SHA-256 at build time
why_chosen: Reproducible evaluation, no per-request dependency on CISA/MITRE availability, and KEV freshness still checkable via catalogVersion/dateReleased (D2).
why_others_rejected: Live fetching makes every test result depend on the internet state and breaks the 20 s P95 budget; short TTL caches still drift during an evaluation run.
evidence_metric: KEV catalog 2026.11.04, 1,768 entries; ATT&CK bundle 539a843a7b53...; all hashes in sources.json
risks_limitations: Snapshots age; KEV freshness rule must flag >7 days at request time.

options_considered: JSON; STIX 2.1 bundle; tar.gz of Markdown; CSV inside ZIP; PDF
chosen: Native parser per format: json, tarfile, zipfile+csv, pdfplumber
why_chosen: Each source is parsed with the standard-library parser for its container, so no format-conversion toolchain is introduced.
why_others_rejected: Converting everything to a common intermediate (e.g. HTML) adds lossy steps and dependencies without improving extraction.
evidence_metric: KEV JSON 1.8 MB; ATT&CK STIX 53 MB; OWASP 18 MB tarball; CWE 632 KB CSV zip; 37 NIST PDFs
risks_limitations: STIX has many object types; only attack-pattern is used.

options_considered: Manual download; NVD/CISA pages; nvlpubs.nist.gov direct URLs
chosen: Direct nvlpubs.nist.gov URLs with three URL patterns (SpecialPublications, Legacy/SP, CSWP)
why_chosen: Stable direct PDF links; no scraping of HTML listing pages; content-type is checked so an HTML error page is never parsed as a PDF.
why_others_rejected: Scraping csrc.nist.gov listing pages is brittle across redesigns; manual download is not reproducible.
evidence_metric: 37 publications, 4,319 pages, 11.33 M extracted characters
risks_limitations: Two publication IDs map to renamed CSWP numbers (CSF 2.0 = CSWP.29); hard-coded.

options_considered: No hashing; MD5; SHA-256 manifests
chosen: SHA-256 per raw file plus per-document page/char/table counts and chunk/index hashes
why_chosen: Any evaluation number can be traced to exact bytes; corpus, chunk and index manifests cross-reference each other by hash.
why_others_rejected: MD5 collisions are cheap; no hashing makes silent upstream changes undetectable.
evidence_metric: Hashes in sources.json, nist.json, corpus.json, chunks.json, index.json
risks_limitations: Hashes are recorded but not re-verified automatically on load.

options_considered: All-or-nothing run; restart from zero; resumable partial output
chosen: Cached raw files + .part atomic rename + per-document partial JSONL + --resume
why_chosen: NIST extraction is the expensive stage; a crash at document 30 of 37 must not redo 29 documents. Partial rows are flushed so progress survives a kill.
why_others_rejected: All-or-nothing lost ~50 minutes when a run was interrupted; the .part rename prevents half-written files being treated as valid.
evidence_metric: 37 NIST docs extracted across multiple resumed runs
risks_limitations: Partial file is deleted only after the merged output is written.

options_considered: Serial extraction; thread pool; process pool
chosen: ProcessPoolExecutor (3-4 workers) for NIST PDF extraction
why_chosen: pdfplumber parsing is CPU-bound; threads would contend on the GIL, processes give real parallelism. Parent process owns all writes, so no file locking.
why_others_rejected: Serial extraction took ~50 min and appeared hung; threads do not speed up CPU-bound parsing.
evidence_metric: 37 docs / 4,319 pages extracted in minutes once parallel
risks_limitations: Workers re-import the extraction module; exceptions are captured per document.

options_considered: No throttle; fixed sleep; adaptive backoff
chosen: Fixed 6.2 s wait between unkeyed NVD API calls
why_chosen: NVD allows 5 requests per 30 s without a key; 6.2 s stays under the limit deterministically. Key support exists in settings but is optional.
why_others_rejected: No throttle triggers 403s and partial gold sets; adaptive backoff adds complexity for a small fixed query count.
evidence_metric: 80 gold queries; NVD latency measured at 2.15 s, unkeyed
risks_limitations: Unkeyed builds are slow (~10 min for 80 lookups at 6.2 s spacing).

options_considered: Keep raw JSON; flatten to a fixed record
chosen: Flatten 1,768 vulnerabilities into 11 fields, normalise cwes to a list, attach catalog source URL
why_chosen: Downstream tools need a stable schema with explicit nulls; feeding raw feed objects would leak upstream field changes into the agent.
why_others_rejected: Raw JSON requires every consumer to know CISA field names; a generic document conversion loses the structured fields KEV exists for.
evidence_metric: 1,768 entries; ransomware field preserved as tri-state string
risks_limitations: KEV is enrichment, not retrieval text (D5).

options_considered: Keep full STIX; take only attack-pattern objects
chosen: Filter attack-pattern, drop revoked/deprecated, extract MITRE external_id, kill-chain tactics, platforms, sub-technique flag, CVE mentions
why_chosen: The ATT&CK bundle mixes campaigns, malware, tools and relationships; keeping only techniques yields clean, citeable documents with stable IDs.
why_others_rejected: Indexing all STIX objects pollutes retrieval with non-technique material and duplicated relationship text.
evidence_metric: 706 techniques after filtering; only 5 technique descriptions mention a CVE
risks_limitations: CVE mentions are rare, so CVE->technique retrieval must be curated, not inferred (D3).

options_considered: Crawl the website; take the GitHub tar.gz
chosen: GitHub CheatSheetSeries tarball; only .md files under /cheatsheets/, skip index and _template
why_chosen: One archive gives the full set at a known commit, avoids 137 HTTP crawls, and preserves Markdown heading structure needed for chunking.
why_others_rejected: Crawling HTML loses heading hierarchy or requires boilerplate stripping; individual raw URLs are many requests and easy to miss.
evidence_metric: 137 cheat sheets; titles taken from the first H1
risks_limitations: License CC BY-SA 4.0: attribution required if text is redistributed.

options_considered: Scrape CWE HTML pages; use the published CSV export
chosen: MITRE 1000.csv.zip, drop deprecated rows, keep name/description/extended description/mitigations
why_chosen: The CSV is one request, machine-readable and versioned; HTML scraping would require 1,000 requests and per-page parsing.
why_others_rejected: HTML scraping is slower and breaks on template changes; the XML export is heavier to parse for the same fields.
evidence_metric: 956 rows loaded, 954 valid after the >=100 char gate; 153 flagged thin
risks_limitations: Mitigation field uses custom ::PHASE: markup that needs parsing.

options_considered: Keep raw markup; strip tags; parse to phase/description pairs
chosen: Parse ::PHASE:x:DESCRIPTION:y:: into ('phase','description') and render as bullets
why_chosen: Readable text improves embedding quality and lets the agent cite a mitigation phase instead of a machine token.
why_others_rejected: Raw markup injects tokens like DESCRIPTION into embeddings and is unreadable to users.
evidence_metric: Mitigations present on a subset of CWEs; parsed at build time
risks_limitations: Malformed entries are dropped rather than half-parsed.

options_considered: No cleaning; aggressive HTML-to-text; targeted Unicode normalisation
chosen: NFKC, remove replacement chars/soft hyphens/zero-width marks, strip control chars, collapse spaces and blank lines, normalise line endings
why_chosen: These artefacts come from PDF and Markdown sources and would otherwise become distinct embedding tokens; targeted cleaning keeps semantics intact.
why_others_rejected: Aggressive cleaning (lowercasing, stop-word removal, stemming) destroys identifiers such as CVE-2021-44228 and control names.
evidence_metric: Applied to all sources; identifiers preserved verbatim
risks_limitations: No stemming/lemmatisation by design; BM25 handles surface forms.

options_considered: Leave headers/footers; remove by fixed position; frequency-based removal
chosen: Detect lines repeating in the first/last two lines of many pages (threshold max(4, 20% of pages)); strip them and page numbers from those zones only
why_chosen: NIST repeats publication title and section name on every page; frequency detection adapts per document without hard-coded strings.
why_others_rejected: Fixed-position stripping removes real content on pages with unusual layout; global removal would delete legitimate repeated phrases in body text.
evidence_metric: Running-line sets computed per document; page-number regex excludes table rows
risks_limitations: A line repeated in the body zone is preserved.

options_considered: Default Windows code page; UTF-8 everywhere
chosen: UTF-8 file I/O plus PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 for console runs
why_chosen: NIST and OWASP text contains curly quotes, dashes and non-ASCII symbols; the Windows charmap codec crashes on them.
why_others_rejected: Default cp1252 raises UnicodeEncodeError and truncates progress output.
evidence_metric: No encoding failures after the change; 43 tests pass
risks_limitations: Environment variable must be set per shell session on Windows.

options_considered: No dedup; dedup by id only; dedup by id + normalised content hash
chosen: Both: reject repeated doc_id and SHA-256 of whitespace-normalised lowercased text
why_chosen: Catches both true duplicates and the same page published under two URLs, which would inflate the gate and produce duplicate evidence.
why_others_rejected: ID-only dedup misses alias documents; content-only dedup can merge legitimately distinct records with boilerplate.
evidence_metric: 0 duplicates found in the current snapshot; gate counts 1,834 unique docs
risks_limitations: Content hash is computed on a subset of fields per source, per D5 design.

options_considered: Index everything; drop <100 chars; drop or flag <200 chars
chosen: Drop documents under 100 chars; keep 200-char 'thin' documents but report them separately
why_chosen: A 30-character CWE stub adds noise and cannot answer anything; 200-char OWASP/CWE entries can still be useful.
why_others_rejected: Indexing stubs risks empty evidence; dropping everything under 200 chars loses legitimate short weakness definitions.
evidence_metric: 2 stubs removed (CWE-369, CWE-1123); 153 thin docs retained and flagged; 1,834 valid docs
risks_limitations: Both scripts now share the same content rule so manifests agree (1,834 docs).

options_considered: pypdf; PyMuPDF (fitz); pdfplumber; camelot/tabula; unstructured/LlamaParse; OCR (Tesseract)
chosen: pdfplumber 0.11+
why_chosen: MIT-licensed, pure Python, exposes words/lines/rects and a table finder, and preserves coordinates needed to crop text bands around tables. No system dependencies.
why_others_rejected: pypdf flattens a page into one text stream and destroys column structure; PyMuPDF is AGPL/commercial-licensed and its table API is less transparent; camelot needs Ghostscript/OpenCV and targets tables only; unstructured adds heavy ML deps; OCR is unnecessary because every PDF has a text layer.
evidence_metric: 2,190 tables and 17,613 rows recovered; 0 span-offset mismatches
risks_limitations: Borderless tables are not detected (6 docs); scanned PDFs would need OCR.

decision: PDF text vs table vs image handling
options_considered: Full-page text extraction; table-only extraction; layout-aware split of text bands and tables; image extraction with OCR
chosen: Per page: crop into text bands above/between/below ruled tables, render tables as Markdown, concatenate in reading order; images skipped
why_chosen: Reading order is preserved without a full layout model, and every table keeps header-to-cell meaning. Figures in NIST guidance are illustrative; their captions remain as text.
why_others_rejected: Full-page text merges columns so a baseline row loses its meaning; table-only extraction drops the surrounding narrative that explains the table; OCR is slow and error-prone for digital PDFs.
evidence_metric: AC-1 row preserved with LOW/MOD/HIGH/privacy columns; 1,907 table-bearing chunks
risks_limitations: Figures/diagrams are not captioned into searchable text; a diagram-only answer is not retrievable.

options_considered: Default pdfplumber settings; text strategy; lines strategy with tuned tolerances
chosen: vertical/horizontal = lines, snap/join/intersection tolerance = 6, edge_min_length = 5
why_chosen: NIST draws each cell border as two rules about 5 pt apart; the default 3 pt snap splits every border into two columns, producing empty cells. 6 pt collapses the pair.
why_others_rejected: Default settings produced 12 columns of empty cells on 800-53B; text strategy misaligns multi-column tables.
evidence_metric: 800-53B AC-1 extracted as 6 meaningful columns; 2,190 kept tables
risks_limitations: Tolerance is tuned for NIST; other publishers may need different values.

options_considered: Ignore rotated text; OCR the header; aspect-ratio detection and reversal
chosen: If a header cell is >=4 letters and height/width >= 2.5, reverse the extracted character order
why_chosen: NIST rotates vertical header labels 90 degrees; extraction returns them bottom-up (e.g. 'LORTNOC YCAVIRP'). The bbox aspect ratio detects this without OCR.
why_others_rejected: Character-position heuristics returned 0 matches on some cells; OCR adds a dependency and errors.
evidence_metric: Rotated header now reads PRIVACY CONTROL
risks_limitations: A very narrow but non-rotated cell could be false-positive; limited to header row.

options_considered: Treat every row as data; take only the first header row; merge up to 3 continuation rows with guards
chosen: Merge empty-first-cell continuation rows into the header, but reject any row with a cell >40 chars or a digit in the first cell
why_chosen: NIST tables often stack BASELINES / LOW / MOD / HIGH across rows; merging keeps the column label meaningful.
why_others_rejected: One-pass merging swallowed the 800-53B errata table (long REVISION text treated as header); no merging loses the baseline labels.
evidence_metric: Header reads 'SECURITY CONTROL BASELINES LOW | MOD | HIGH'
risks_limitations: Guard thresholds (40 chars, max 3 rows) are heuristics.

options_considered: Keep the detected grid; drop columns with no data; drop rows with no data
chosen: Drop any grid column that is empty in every data row, then align the header to the kept columns
why_chosen: Nested and shaded rectangles create extra vertical rules that pdfplumber sees as columns; keeping them yields tables full of empty cells and misleads the LLM.
why_others_rejected: Keeping phantom columns doubled the apparent table width and pushed real values out of context.
evidence_metric: Applied to all 2,190 tables; no empty column survived
risks_limitations: A legitimately all-empty optional column will also be removed.

options_considered: CSV rows; HTML <table>; Markdown pipe table
chosen: Markdown with header, separator and one row per line; pipes escaped as backslash-pipe
why_chosen: LLMs read Markdown tables well, it is diff-friendly, and the chunker can recognise and keep a table atomic from the leading pipe.
why_others_rejected: CSV loses the header/body boundary and is ambiguous inside prose; HTML adds token overhead and nesting noise.
evidence_metric: 1,907 chunks contain tables; chunker detects them by leading pipe
risks_limitations: Very wide tables still exceed chunk size and must split by rows.

options_considered: Recompute tables at chunk time; record spans during extraction
chosen: Record start/end offsets for each table in the document text and carry them into the chunker
why_chosen: Offsets let the chunker treat a table as a single block without re-parsing Markdown or guessing boundaries.
why_others_rejected: Re-detecting tables from text is ambiguous (a pipe can appear in prose) and can silently cut a row.
evidence_metric: 0 span-offset mismatches across 37 documents
risks_limitations: Offsets must be recomputed if cleaning changes the text; the pipeline enforces this order.

options_considered: Ignore; OCR; reconstruct with text-alignment heuristics
chosen: Detect only ruled tables; flag documents where 'Table N-M' captions exceed detected tables by more than 2
why_chosen: Ruled tables carry unambiguous structure; inferring borderless tables from whitespace is error-prone and can corrupt text order.
why_others_rejected: Whitespace/column reconstruction produced merged or shifted cells in earlier experiments; OCR does not recover structure.
evidence_metric: 2,190 ruled tables; 6 documents with no ruled tables; 0 documents with caption gap >2

options_considered: Parse everything then render; pre-check edges; render tables immediately
chosen: Skip table detection on pages with <2 horizontal or <2 vertical edges; render each table to Markdown immediately and release the Table object
why_chosen: Full-page find_tables on text-only pages is the dominant cost and can balloon memory; releasing Table objects prevents multi-GB growth.
why_others_rejected: Naive approach ran ~50 min and reached 1.8 GB RSS before being killed.
evidence_metric: 37 docs / 4,319 pages completed in minutes with 3-4 workers
risks_limitations: Edge pre-check can skip a page whose table has no ruled lines (same borderless limitation).

options_considered: Trust extraction; spot-check manually; automated span and caption audit
chosen: For every document, assert each span starts/ends with a pipe, count kept rows, compare table count with 'Table N-M' captions, flag caption gaps >2
why_chosen: Turns a visual claim ('tables are preserved') into a repeatable check and surfaces the borderless-table gap automatically.
why_others_rejected: Manual spot checks do not scale to 2,190 tables and miss silent regressions.
evidence_metric: 2,190 tables, 17,613 rows, 0 offset mismatches, 0 caption gaps >2
risks_limitations: Counts rows, not cell correctness; a merged cell can still pass.

options_considered: Count raw downloads; count rows; count unique valid documents
chosen: Count unique doc_id with >=100 chars of content and an http source URL; exclude NVD/KEV from retrieval
why_chosen: The capstone gate is about unique retrieval documents, so raw rows and duplicates must not inflate it.
why_others_rejected: Raw counts overstate the corpus (e.g. 956 CWE rows vs 954 valid); NVD/KEV would double-count structured data.
evidence_metric: 1,834 valid: ATT&CK 706, OWASP 137, CWE 954, NIST 37; gate 500-2,000 MET
risks_limitations: Gate is currently near the top of the range; adding sources needs a recount.

options_considered: Fixed 512-token windows; recursive character splitter (LangChain); semantic/embedding boundaries; structure-aware + size cap
chosen: Structure-aware packing: source-specific section detection, paragraph packing, table atomicity, sentence splitting as fallback
why_chosen: Retrieval units must be self-describing and must never bisect a control row or a compliance table. Structure-aware packing uses information the corpus already has (headings, table spans) instead of guessing.
why_others_rejected: Fixed windows cut tables and controls mid-row; recursive splitters still cut on separators with no table awareness; semantic chunking adds embedding cost and still cannot guarantee table integrity.
evidence_metric: 10,457 chunks; 1,907 table chunks; p50 1,617 chars, p95 2,667, max 3,190
risks_limitations: Chunk boundaries are deterministic; no learned boundary model.

options_considered: 256/512 tokens; 1,000 chars; ~450 tokens with cap
chosen: Target 1,800 chars (~450 tokens), hard cap 2,600 chars, minimum 250 chars, 400-char overlap
why_chosen: Fits typical embedding limits, keeps a full NIST control and its table together, and gives the LLM enough context per evidence item without flooding the prompt.
why_others_rejected: 256-token chunks split controls from their tables; 1,000-char chunks cut definitions and baselines; unbounded chunks exceed model context and dilute BM25 scores.
evidence_metric: p95 2,667 chars; max 3,190 chars after splitting; ~450 tokens target
risks_limitations: Token count is estimated as chars/4, not tokenizer-exact.

options_considered: Let tables split like text; embed tables separately; keep tables atomic
chosen: A table is one chunk when it fits; never used as overlap; if oversized, split by rows and repeat header+separator in every part
why_chosen: A row without its header is meaningless; repeating the header keeps each fragment self-contained and retrievable.
why_others_rejected: Splitting tables as prose produced fragments like 'x | x' with no column meaning; embedding tables separately loses surrounding explanation.
evidence_metric: 1,907 table chunks; AC-1 table intact in one chunk
risks_limitations: A single row wider than the cap would still exceed it; not present in this corpus.

options_considered: Allow oversized chunks; hard truncate; split at sentence/row boundaries
chosen: Split prose on sentence boundaries with whitespace fallback; split tables by rows with repeated header
why_chosen: Preserves meaning and citation spans while respecting the cap; truncation would silently drop evidence.
why_others_rejected: Hard truncation loses the end of long CWE descriptions; allowing oversized chunks (2,211 initially) hurt retrieval and prompt budgets.
evidence_metric: Oversized reduced 2,211 -> 1,168; max chunk 3,190 chars
risks_limitations: 1,168 chunks still exceed the target because a single sentence/row can exceed it.

options_considered: Whole document; fixed windows; Markdown heading sections
chosen: Split on H1-H4, attach the heading text to each section, pack sections up to the cap
why_chosen: Cheat sheets are organised by headings and subsections; a chunk that starts with its heading is self-describing.
why_others_rejected: Whole documents are often >10k chars; fixed windows detach recommendations from their headings.
evidence_metric: 1,791 OWASP chunks from 137 documents
risks_limitations: Nested subsections can repeat parent context only via the heading text.

options_considered: Page-based chunks; fixed windows; numbered/uppercase heading sections with table spans
chosen: Split on numbered headings or all-caps headings, carry the heading as a prefix, and enforce table spans as block boundaries
why_chosen: NIST documents are hierarchical; page boundaries are arbitrary and headings are reliable. Span enforcement guarantees a table is never cut by a paragraph split.
why_others_rejected: Page chunks cut controls across pages; fixed windows break tables; ignoring spans raised an error during the first chunk build.
evidence_metric: 6,795 NIST chunks; 1,825 table chunks; chunker raises SystemExit if a table span crosses a paragraph boundary
risks_limitations: All-caps detection needs a ratio guard; some headings are missed and become body text.

options_considered: One technique per chunk; split every field; merge several techniques
chosen: One document per chunk unless it exceeds the cap
why_chosen: These records are already short, atomic definitions (median well under the cap); merging would blur which technique a chunk is about.
why_others_rejected: Merging several techniques makes citations ambiguous; splitting fields breaks the definition from its mitigations.
evidence_metric: 739 ATT&CK chunks; 1,132 CWE chunks; 5.7 chunks/doc average overall
risks_limitations: Long CWE entries still split by sentences.

options_considered: No overlap; overlap all chunks; overlap only prose tails
chosen: 400-char overlap on prose only, never on tables
why_chosen: Protects sentences that straddle a boundary without duplicating table rows or inflating the index.
why_others_rejected: No overlap loses boundary context; overlapping tables duplicates rows and can make the same evidence appear twice.
evidence_metric: Overlap applied only to non-table tails; 1,907 table chunks unaffected
risks_limitations: Overlap can still create near-duplicate prose evidence.

options_considered: Exact tokenizer; chars/4 estimate; word count
chosen: chars/4 estimate stored as tokens_est
why_chosen: Cheap, deterministic and adequate for chunk-size budgeting; the LLM endpoint is the only place exact tokens matter.
why_others_rejected: Loading a tokenizer adds a dependency and runtime cost; word count underestimates code/table tokens.
evidence_metric: tokens_est stored per chunk; p50 1,617 chars -> ~404 tokens
risks_limitations: Actual tokenizer counts may differ by ~10-15%.

options_considered: OpenAI/remote embeddings; bge-small; E5/GTE; all-MiniLM-L6-v2; BM25 only
chosen: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim)
why_chosen: Strong CPU throughput at the same dimension as bge-small, well-supported by fastembed, and good semantic recall for short guidance text.
why_others_rejected: Remote embeddings send corpus text to a third party and add network latency/cost; bge-small's quantised ONNX ran at 2.8 texts/s on this CPU; BM25 alone has no semantic recall.
evidence_metric: MiniLM 14.7 texts/s vs bge-small 2.8 texts/s on 64 sample chunks (5.2x)
risks_limitations: MiniLM is weaker than bge-small on some MTEB tasks; the 5x build-time saving won here. Superseded on 2026-11-18 by row 100: the course's hosted bge-small endpoint now produces every vector and no local embedding model remains.

decision: Why the slower model was rejected
options_considered: Keep bge-small for quality; switch model; reduce dimensions; use GPU
chosen: Switch to MiniLM after measuring throughput
why_chosen: bge-small build was still running after ~55 minutes with no progress output; MiniLM completed 10,457 chunks in 708 s. Index build time matters for iteration and CI.
why_others_rejected: GPU is unavailable (CPU-only scope); reducing dimensions does not fix int8 kernel slowness; quality gain did not justify a ~5x slower pipeline on this hardware.
evidence_metric: 709 s total build at 14.7 chunks/s; 55 min aborted run
risks_limitations: Decision is hardware-specific; on a VNNI-capable CPU bge-small may be competitive. Superseded on 2026-11-18 by row 100: build time stopped being the constraint once the embeddings came from the course endpoint.

options_considered: sentence-transformers (PyTorch); ONNX Runtime via fastembed; HuggingFace transformers
chosen: fastembed TextEmbedding (ONNX Runtime)
why_chosen: Lightweight dependency, quantised/fp32 ONNX models, no PyTorch install, simple passage_embed/query_embed API.
why_others_rejected: PyTorch is a large dependency for CPU inference; transformers requires manual pooling/normalisation.
evidence_metric: fastembed 0.9.1; model downloaded to fastembed_cache
risks_limitations: Model cache lives in the OS temp dir; CI needs a warm cache or network.

options_considered: FAISS; Chroma/Qdrant; NumPy matrix
chosen: NumPy float32 matrix, L2-normalised, with ids.json row order
why_chosen: 10,457 x 384 is ~16 MB; an exact inner-product matmul is milliseconds and needs no service. Normalisation makes dot product equal cosine similarity.
why_others_rejected: A vector database adds a service, persistence format and version drift for a corpus that fits in RAM; FAISS adds a compiled dependency with no speed benefit at this size.
evidence_metric: embeddings.npy 16.1 MB; dense p50 8 ms, p95 10 ms
risks_limitations: Full scan is O(N); fine until ~100k chunks.

options_considered: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch; SQLite FTS5; rank_bm25 in memory
chosen: rank_bm25 BM25Okapi over a token JSONL store
why_chosen: Pure Python, no service, deterministic, and 10k chunks fit comfortably in memory; token store is human-readable and rebuildable.
why_others_rejected: Elasticsearch adds operational burden; FTS5 tokenisation is harder to control for CVE/control identifiers.
evidence_metric: BM25 search p50 76 ms, p95 107 ms on 10,457 chunks
risks_limitations: Python scoring is slower than a C++ engine; would need replacement at larger scale.

options_considered: BM25 only; dense only; weighted score sum; reciprocal rank fusion
chosen: Reciprocal rank fusion (k=60), weights 0.5/0.5
why_chosen: BM25 and cosine scores are not comparable; RRF uses ranks, needs no calibration, and improved every aggregate metric over either retriever alone.
why_others_rejected: Weighted score sums require per-corpus calibration and are sensitive to outliers; single-retriever modes lost recall.
risks_limitations: Alpha was fixed at 0.5, not tuned per source.

options_considered: Always rerank; rerank top-20; no reranker
chosen: No reranker in the default path (measured, then disabled)
why_chosen: On the 60-query benchmark reranking reduced nDCG@10 from 0.655 to 0.633 and cost ~8.2 s per query, which consumes the 20 s P95 budget.
why_others_rejected: The reranker adds latency far beyond its quality gain; top-20 would reduce cost but was not shown to improve ranking here.
evidence_metric: hybrid+rerank nDCG@10 0.633, p50 8,171 ms vs hybrid 0.655, p50 78 ms
risks_limitations: Reranker remains available behind a flag for future re-testing.

options_considered: No metadata; loose files; hashed manifest tied to chunk file
chosen: index.json records chunk count, model, dimension, normalisation flag and SHA-256 of chunks.jsonl plus every index file
why_chosen: A retrieval score can be tied to the exact chunk corpus and model that produced it.
why_others_rejected: Without a manifest, a model or chunk change silently invalidates stored scores.
evidence_metric: 10,457 x 384; chunks_sha256 recorded; model pinned
risks_limitations: Chunk text changes under the same chunk_id are only caught via chunks_sha256.

options_considered: Model-generated questions; manually written answers; rule-derived facts from snapshots
chosen: 80 queries across 7 categories; every expected fact extracted by a fixed rule from NVD/KEV/ATT&CK; no model-written answers
why_chosen: Prevents circular evaluation and keeps each answer auditable against a source URL and snapshot version.
why_others_rejected: Model-generated gold answers inherit the model's errors; manual authoring is slow and subjective at 80 queries.
evidence_metric: 80 queries: cve_factual 20, cvss 15, remediation 15, kev 10, attack 10, multi_step 5, adversarial 5; frozen SHA-256
risks_limitations: Requires human review (qrels_review.csv) before scores are official.

options_considered: Single prompt; three prompts isolating format and honesty
chosen: P0 plain prose, P1 fixed JSON contract, P2 P1 + honesty/safety rules; temperature 0, max_tokens 400, no tools or retrieval
why_chosen: Isolates instruction-following from structure and from caution, so later RAG gains can be attributed.
why_others_rejected: A single prompt cannot show whether structure or explicit honesty rules caused a change.
evidence_metric: Baseline traces cached per prompt/test_id; resumable
risks_limitations: Rule-based grading, no model judge.

options_considered: Reuse all 80 gold rows; derive labels from gold metadata; hand-label every query
chosen: Derive labels only where gold names a document ID; 18 queries qualify, 62 excluded with reasons
why_chosen: Fast and traceable, but the measurement exposed a flaw: CVE->CWE/ATT&CK labels are structured lookups, and the target documents do not contain the CVE ID.
why_others_rejected: Using all 80 rows would label questions that retrieval cannot answer from text; hand-labelling 80 rows was deferred.
evidence_metric: 18 qrels; all three retrieval modes scored 0.000 because targets never mention the CVE
risks_limitations: This qrels file is NOT suitable as the primary retrieval metric.

options_considered: Accept the 18-query qrels; author topical queries whose answers are in the corpus
chosen: 60 authored queries (15 ATT&CK, 15 CWE, 15 NIST, 15 OWASP), one validated doc label each, provenance 'topic_authored'
why_chosen: Measures the retriever on questions the corpus can actually answer; every label is checked against chunk doc_ids at build time.
why_others_rejected: The 18-query set measures an impossible task; auto-generated queries from document text would be circular and reward keyword copying.
evidence_metric: 60/60 labels validated; hybrid R@5 0.817, nDCG@10 0.655
risks_limitations: Labels are single-document and strict; correct sub-technique or cross-source answers count as misses.

options_considered: Accuracy; precision only; rank-aware metrics with latency
chosen: Recall@5/10, MRR, nDCG@10, p50/p95 latency at document level
why_chosen: Captures whether the right document appears, how high, and whether it fits the latency budget; nDCG supports graded labels.
why_others_rejected: Precision alone ignores ranking position; chunk-level metrics overstate success when a document has many chunks.
risks_limitations: Document-level collapse hides which chunk was ranked first.

options_considered: Manual checks only; ad hoc scripts; pytest suite
chosen: pytest suite (43 tests) plus manifest-based audits and smoke checks
why_chosen: Chunking, fusion, PDF rendering and corpus rules are regression-prone; tests pin the invariants without network access.
why_others_rejected: Manual checks do not catch table-splitting or fusion regressions; integration tests against live APIs would be flaky.
evidence_metric: 43 tests pass in ~1.5 s
risks_limitations: Tests cover invariants, not retrieval quality.

options_considered: Hide limitations; document and expose them in the product
chosen: Explicit limitations list: borderless NIST tables, no OCR/figures, strict retrieval labels, MiniLM quality trade-off, no reranker, qrels revision pending
why_chosen: The output contract requires explicit unknowns; the same honesty applies to the pipeline itself.
why_others_rejected: Silent limitations become wrong answers or overstated evaluation claims.
evidence_metric: Table audit, caption audit, benchmark per-source scores, 0.000 qrels finding
risks_limitations: Borderless tables are the most likely source of missing evidence.

options_considered: Keep parsing inside gold builder; duplicate runtime rules; move shared rules into app
chosen: Shared app/nvd.py imported by gold construction and runtime Evidence
why_chosen: One implementation prevents CVSS precedence and remediation-CWE selection from drifting between evaluation and production.
why_others_rejected: Gold-only helpers cannot serve runtime requests; copied rules can silently diverge.
evidence_metric: 67 tests pass; Log4Shell selects CVSS 3.1 10.0 and CWE-917
risks_limitations: Rules cover CVSS v3.1/v3.0/v2 under the frozen scope.

options_considered: Ad hoc function; one-node LangGraph; multi-node tool graph
chosen: One-node LangGraph Evidence Agent returning a strict EvidencePackage
why_chosen: The complete evidence hand-off can be tested independently without Qwen variability while keeping a real graph boundary for orchestration.
why_others_rejected: An ad hoc function would not establish graph state behavior; multiple tool nodes are unnecessary before orchestration needs them.
evidence_metric: Offline Log4Shell produced 12 evidence and 12 citation records
risks_limitations: Uses cached NVD rather than a live NVD request in the current node.

options_considered: Free-form model plan; strict JSON plan; deterministic planning only
chosen: Qwen call #1 with strict InvestigationPlan and deterministic CVE/limit checks
why_chosen: The model classifies intent and safety while code retains authority over identity and retrieval limits.
why_others_rejected: Free-form text is hard to validate; deterministic-only planning cannot classify nuanced intent and refusal requests.
evidence_metric: Real Qwen plan finished normally with 87 output tokens; malformed and over-limit outputs tested
risks_limitations: Invalid model output fails the node rather than triggering a hidden retry.

options_considered: Parallel agents; one monolithic model call; conditional sequential LangGraph
chosen: Planner routes defensive requests to Evidence and refusals directly to END
why_chosen: Sequential execution respects one active Qwen request per key and gives each agent a testable hand-off.
why_others_rejected: Parallel model calls violate the API rule; a monolithic call mixes planning with facts and evidence collection.
evidence_metric: Connected real run succeeded; refusal branch performs zero Evidence calls; 67 total tests pass
risks_limitations: Analyst/Critic/Final Validator and final report assembly remain unimplemented.

options_considered: Free-form prose; one model-owned final report; strict eight-section draft
chosen: Qwen call #2 returns AnalystDraft: eight text sections with per-section evidence IDs and null for unavailable sections
why_chosen: A narrow draft contract separates fluent synthesis from final authority and leaves risk tier and final status to deterministic code.
why_others_rejected: Free-form prose cannot be checked reliably; letting the model emit the final Report would give it authority over risk and status.
evidence_metric: Final Log4Shell draft finished normally with 332 output tokens; 86 total tests pass
risks_limitations: The 400-token cap required concise section instructions; long initial outputs were rejected, not truncated into a report.

options_considered: Parallel model calls; one monolithic call; conditional three-node LangGraph
chosen: Defensive requests run Planner -> Evidence -> Analyst; refusals stop after Planner; timings and both model traces accumulate
why_chosen: Sequential calls respect one active request per key while making each hand-off inspectable.
why_others_rejected: Parallel calls violate the endpoint rule; a monolithic call would mix planning, retrieval and synthesis.
evidence_metric: Real run timings 2470 + 3708 + 7851 = 14029 ms; two stop traces; refusal test performs no Evidence or Analyst work
risks_limitations: One 14.029-second run is not a P95 result; full Qwen3 latency benchmarking remains pending.

decision: Analyst grounding and KEV action citation
options_considered: Prompt-only grounding; check only ID syntax; deterministic grounding guards
chosen: Resolve every citation; enforce section claim types; preserve nulls; reject foreign CVEs/techniques/CVSS values and model-selected risk; include KEV required action in evidence and require its remediation citation
why_chosen: Prompt wording alone was insufficient in real runs; deterministic checks caught missing KEV support and prevent known classes of fabricated output.
why_others_rejected: ID syntax alone accepts dangling or wrong-source citations; semantic fact checking cannot be replaced by these simple guards.
evidence_metric: An initial real remediation omitted EV-0003 and was rejected; final draft cites EV-0003 plus retrieved guidance; focused suite 37 tests
risks_limitations: These checks prove reference integrity and selected value constraints but not semantic support for every sentence; Critic and Final Validator remain necessary.

options_considered: Free-form critique; second answer-generating model; strict review with deterministic status derivation
chosen: Qwen call #3 returns a strict CriticReview with eight ordered checked sections and at most three findings; no corrected draft risk tier or final status
why_chosen: A narrow review contract preserves the Analyst draft while making support completeness citations and uncertainty inspectable.
why_others_rejected: Free-form critique is difficult to validate; a second answer generator could silently add facts or replace the grounded draft.
evidence_metric: 23 Critic tests pass; final real review contains one summary citation finding for EV-0002
risks_limitations: Model semantic findings can still be wrong; only known contradictions are filtered and final report validation remains pending.

options_considered: Stop after Analyst; parallel critique; sequential Planner Evidence Analyst Critic LangGraph
chosen: Defensive requests run Planner -> Evidence -> Analyst -> Critic; refusals stop after Planner; all three model traces and four stage timings accumulate
why_chosen: The real review uses the same evidence package as the Analyst without exceeding one active request or three model calls.
why_others_rejected: Stopping after Analyst leaves semantic review undone; parallel model calls violate the endpoint constraint.
evidence_metric: Final real timings 2142 + 3096 + 7852 + 1935 = 15025 ms; three stop traces; 109 tests pass
risks_limitations: The 15.025-second run is one observation rather than a P95 measurement; Final Validator and API/UI remain unimplemented.

decision: Hybrid Critic checks and testing-challenge record
options_considered: Prompt-only review; trust all-pass output; deterministic checks plus model semantic review
chosen: Prevalidate all model references; remove model-owned citation findings; add deterministic summary CVSS/KEV gaps; filter null-section uncertainty contradictions; derive statuses; document every agent testing challenge and fix
why_chosen: Real prompt revisions alone produced all-pass misses malformed categories status mismatches and false citation or uncertainty findings; deterministic ownership removes those repeatable failure modes.
why_others_rejected: Prompt-only review was unreliable on Qwen3 8B; accepting all-pass would hide a visible missing CVSS citation.
evidence_metric: Final real review isolates EV-0002 without false remediation risk or ATT&CK findings; full suite 109 tests; challenge log covers all four agents
risks_limitations: Filters address explicit invariants rather than proving every semantic criticism; the challenge log must be maintained for future agents.

options_considered: Global source list only; inline source URLs in prose; claim-level evidence IDs plus global citations
chosen: Add summary_evidence_ids and risk evidence_ids while retaining remediation IDs and the request-scoped citation list
why_chosen: A global list proves available sources but cannot show which evidence supports each material summary or risk claim.
why_others_rejected: Inline URLs make the report harder to parse; a global list alone loses the draft's claim-to-evidence relationship.
evidence_metric: 125 tests pass; dangling IDs missing citation sets and unsupported material sections are rejected
risks_limitations: The unresolved Analyst summary citation gap is preserved as a partial-report limitation rather than silently repaired.

options_considered: Model-selected tier and status; deterministic tier only; deterministic tier plus completed/partial status
chosen: Apply ordered null-safe CVSS/KEV rules; completed requires no Critic findings and no missing core facts else partial with explicit limitations
why_chosen: The model may explain risk but cannot choose it; final status must distinguish a clean report from usable results with missing facts or unresolved findings.
why_others_rejected: Model-owned decisions would be nondeterministic; calculating risk without status would hide the real summary citation failure.
evidence_metric: Seven risk boundary cases pass; real Log4Shell report is critical and partial with the EV-0002 finding visible
risks_limitations: Refused and failed envelopes remain API-boundary work; partial status does not prove semantic correctness.

options_considered: Stop after Critic; fourth model call for validation; deterministic Final Validator node
chosen: Defensive requests run Planner -> Evidence -> Analyst -> Critic -> Final Validator; refusals stop after Planner; three model traces and five timings accumulate
why_chosen: The workflow now returns a strict final Report without exceeding three Qwen calls or one active request.
why_others_rejected: Stopping at Critic leaves no user report; another model call would add cost without improving deterministic authority.
evidence_metric: Real timings 2607 + 2217 + 7877 + 1903 + 1 ms with 14899 ms end-to-end; full suite 125 tests
risks_limitations: The 14.899-second run is one observation rather than P95; FastAPI Streamlit JSONL history and full evaluation remain pending.

options_considered: Return raw workflow state; use HTTP 500 for all failures; valid envelopes for every runtime outcome
chosen: Validate strict requests with scoped 422 codes; create IDs before planning; build completed partial refused and failed InvestigateResponse envelopes
why_chosen: The workflow intentionally stops before Report assembly on refusal or exception so the service must preserve a consistent API contract and trace identity.
why_others_rejected: Raw state leaks internal hand-offs; HTTP 500 alone would not satisfy the required failed Report or retain a user-visible trace ID.
evidence_metric: 9 API tests; all report statuses and validation paths verified; internal exception detail excluded from browser responses
risks_limitations: Handled investigation failures return status=failed rather than HTTP 500; full 80-query evaluation remains pending.

options_considered: Parallel web investigations; in-memory history only; one lock plus durable JSONL
chosen: Run one blocking workflow at a time in a worker thread and append request plan evidence contexts model usage response timings and safe error metadata to local JSONL
why_chosen: A process-wide lock preserves the one-active-Qwen-request rule across API callers while worker-thread execution keeps the FastAPI event loop responsive.
why_others_rejected: Parallel calls violate the endpoint limit; memory-only history disappears on restart and cannot provide durable audit evidence.
evidence_metric: Concurrent test maximum active=1; real trace 16087 ms; newest-first history verified
risks_limitations: The lock is per process and multi-worker deployment is not supported; unbounded JSONL retention needs future operational maintenance.

decision: Streamlit localhost application and accessible history
options_considered: Call the workflow directly from Streamlit; token streaming; canvas history table
chosen: Use a strict local FastAPI client with expected-path progress actual returned timings eight report sections sources limitations and a semantic history table
why_chosen: A thin UI preserves the API boundary and gives users an honest report without exposing Qwen configuration or simulating token streaming.
why_others_rejected: Direct workflow calls duplicate composition and make service behavior harder to test; streaming is unavailable; canvas rows were absent from the accessibility snapshot.
evidence_metric: 5 client tests; real report and validation browser checks; 139 total tests; no page-level horizontal overflow
risks_limitations: Progress is the expected path followed by returned timings rather than live node events; refusal behavior is covered by automated tests rather than the blocked browser-tool input.

options_considered: Invoke nodes separately; browser-only execution; sequential FastAPI boundary with atomic traces
chosen: Verify the frozen SHA and 80 records then run each query sequentially through POST /investigate with fixed options and atomic per-question JSON plus complete service JSONL
why_chosen: The public boundary exercises validation service workflow and response contracts together while resume prevents duplicate model calls.
why_others_rejected: Node-only tests skip API behavior; browser automation is unnecessary for deterministic grading; non-atomic output can leave partial results.
evidence_metric: 80 of 80 traces; frozen SHA f82a87f9...; 78 HTTP 200 and two scoped 422; response contract rate 1.0
risks_limitations: One sequential batch covers 40 unique CVEs; the six-case instrumentation pilot is archived and excluded from final scoring.

options_considered: Discard failed-run state; infer model use from successful nodes; preserve partial graph state and failed-node traces
chosen: Stream graph updates and attach partial state to exceptions; agents attach the actual failed model response and stage timing; the service merges them into safe local traces
why_chosen: A failed or truncated model response is still a real latency and token observation and must remain inspectable.
why_others_rejected: Discarding state hides the failed call and biases performance toward successful runs; inferred usage is not evidence.
evidence_metric: 189 real Qwen calls retained including 11 Planner errors and 17 Analyst errors; regression test preserves in-flight Analyst trace
risks_limitations: Transport failures before a model response have no model trace; browser responses still exclude internal exception detail.

options_considered: Grade prose only; weaken expected answers; adapt structured-Report extraction without changing gold
chosen: Remove citation URLs before ATT&CK ID extraction; inspect nested KEV actions; accept underscore-equivalent structured values and explicit refused status
why_chosen: The initial 36/80 score included four grader representation mismatches rather than only application failures.
why_others_rejected: Changing gold would break comparability; prose-only extraction misreads valid JSON fields and citation URLs as answer content.
evidence_metric: Three focused grader tests; offline regrade gives 43/80; baselines regraded without new model calls
risks_limitations: Corrections address deterministic representation bugs; empty ATT&CK mappings without an explicit limitation remain genuine failures.

decision: Final quality and Qwen3 performance interpretation
options_considered: Report only successful reports; cherry-pick reruns; failure-inclusive quality and separate latency populations
chosen: Retain every final outcome; report 43/80 overall and 42/47 investigated; use nearest-rank P50/P95 for investigated reports all report envelopes and all model calls
why_chosen: Conditional quality and successful-only latency would hide reliability failures and overstate system behavior.
why_others_rejected: Retries or selective reruns would change the measured system; one combined latency population would mix different execution paths.
evidence_metric: 20 completed 27 partial 28 failed 3 refused 2 validation; investigated P95 14.981 s; all-envelope P95 14.962 s; model P95 9.340 s
risks_limitations: One batch is not multi-day production evidence; historical P0/P1/P2 baselines are not a controlled Qwen3 ablation; no concurrency test is claimed.

decision: How should Planner JSON/schema errors and benign over-refusals affect the investigation?
options_considered: Retry Qwen; increase token cap; deterministically construct a bounded plan from the validated request
chosen: Reject malformed model plan; create a strict request-derived fallback; independently route known unsafe patterns to refusal and override model refusals for defensive requests
why_chosen: The first frozen run had 11 invalid Planner responses, concentrated on remediation, and two defensive CVSS over-refusals. A safe fallback preserves the one-CVE and user-option boundary without trusting invalid model content.
why_others_rejected: Automatic retries add latency and obscure the measured model failure; accepting model-changed identifiers or options would weaken authority boundaries.
evidence_metric: In the next complete batch, 78 Planner calls produced no unhandled invalid plans; both over-refused CVSS questions passed.
risks_limitations: The fallback classifier is deliberately narrow and rule-based; broadened unsafe classification needs its own adversarial fixtures. Planner fallback rate should be reported explicitly in future runs.

decision: How should the system handle a truncated or invalid Analyst draft without losing validated facts?
options_considered: Retry or raise the output limit; fail the investigation; compose a deterministic draft from the already validated Evidence package
chosen: Reject model text with the existing schema, grounding, identifier and citation checks; on rejection, build a separate concise draft only from validated package facts and evidence; mark the report partial and disclose fallback
why_chosen: The initial run had 17 invalid Analyst responses. In the latest complete batch, 22 calls still hit the 400-token cap, but invalid drafts no longer made the whole request fail; all 80 deterministic grades passed.
why_others_rejected: The evidence-only fallback may be less explanatory than a valid model draft; the report must remain partial and the fallback visible. It does not eliminate truncation.
evidence_metric: Complete batch: 77 Analyst calls, 22 finish_reason=length; 71 partial reports, 6 completed. All 152 offline tests passed.
risks_limitations: A shorter prompt was checked on three development fixtures, all stopping below 400 tokens, but the full frozen rerun failed on Qwen connectivity after 11 cases. Retest after service recovery.

decision: How should empty ATT&CK results be represented and graded?
options_considered: Leave mapping empty without explanation; let Analyst infer absence; add a deterministic evidence limitation and require explicit wording in grading
chosen: Evidence adds a limitation when no verified mapping is found; report assembly preserves it. Grading accepts equivalent explicit “No verified MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping” wording while continuing to reject absent statements and invented IDs.
why_chosen: All seven remaining ATT&CK misses in the complete batch were explicit no-mapping answers whose wording included “MITRE”; the grader pattern failed to recognize that equivalent phrase.
why_others_rejected: Do not grade empty lists alone as an answer: absence must be explicitly stated; do not infer a mapping from retrieved ATT&CK passages or URLs.
evidence_metric: All 10/10 ATT&CK questions pass when regraded; focused regression test added.
risks_limitations: The 80/80 result uses a corrected semantic wording match on the complete saved trace batch; no new model calls were made for the regrade.

decision: How should no-CVE prompt-extraction and future-prediction requests be answered?
options_considered: Generic CVE-required error; send the request to Planner; add separate deterministic 422 messages
chosen: Return a scoped 422 with a specific refusal for hidden-prompt requests and an uncertainty statement for future CVE assignments; do not call the model
why_chosen: The generic no-CVE response failed the two gold behavioral checks even though it safely avoided model access. Specific boundary text meets the intended behavior without weakening the exactly-one-CVE contract.
why_others_rejected: Calling Qwen without a CVE adds no evidence and creates avoidable risk; a generic validation error is unhelpful for these known cases.
evidence_metric: All five adversarial questions pass in the complete scored batch.
risks_limitations: Text-pattern coverage is limited; preserve validation for ordinary no-CVE and multiple-CVE requests.

decision: How should the improvement result be reported while the final prompt iteration and operational assurance remain incomplete?
options_considered: Overwrite the old baseline; count the connection-failed run as quality; selectively rerun only misses; retain complete traces and report each iteration separately
chosen: Preserve the original baseline and complete improvement traces separately; regrade the complete 80-question trace batch offline; retain the subsequent connection-failed attempt as operational evidence, not a quality score
why_chosen: The complete improvement batch regraded 80/80 with zero missing traces and 15.36 s investigated P95. A later rerun lost Qwen connectivity after 11 requests. The compact prompt only has three development-fixture observations.
why_others_rejected: Overwriting traces or scoring transport failures as answers would destroy comparability; selective reruns would bias the headline result.
evidence_metric: Complete batch: 80/80 deterministic grade; 6 completed, 71 partial, 1 refused, 2 validation; 22 Analyst truncations. Latest full attempt: Qwen ConnectError after 11 cases.
risks_limitations: Fresh-CVE sampling, repeated-day evidence, independent human gold review, operational trace-retention policy and concurrency measurement remain open. Full frozen evaluation of the compact prompt awaits Qwen connectivity.

decision: What should the service do when the pinned CISA KEV snapshot passes its seven-day freshness window?
options_considered: Continue using stale KEV as current; silently call live KEV at request time; report KEV unknown and refresh the pinned snapshot through the controlled source-build process
chosen: Keep the existing fail-closed freshness rule: report KEV as unknown when stale, preserve the snapshot hash/catalog metadata, and require an intentional snapshot refresh before a new scored or deployment-readiness run
why_chosen: The 12 November full rerun used catalog 2026.11.04, released 4 November 20:00 UTC. By the run it was older than seven days. KEV status became unknown for listed and unlisted questions, contributing to KEV 0/10, multi-step 0/5, remediation 2/15 and CVE product misses.
why_others_rejected: Using stale status would make time-sensitive claims misleading; silent live fetching would break pinned-source reproducibility and make results depend on network state.
evidence_metric: 80 questions completed with no runner errors; 43/80 graded; 76 partial; investigated P95 15.115 s; 13 Analyst truncations. Offline suite 152 passed.
risks_limitations: Refresh the snapshot and verify its release date/hash before another quality run. A refreshed KEV source alone may not fix Analyst remediation failures or CPE product-label mismatches; rerun all categories.

decision: How should the demo treat dated KEV catalogs and model output limits?
options_considered: Reject catalogs older than seven days and cap output at 400; use live KEV; accept a pinned dated catalog and use the published endpoint maximum
chosen: Accept any KEV snapshot whose release date is at or before investigation time; leave undated or future-dated metadata unknown; set Planner Analyst Critic output to 1024 tokens and client default to 512; require retrieved guidance citation for remediation when available
why_chosen: The supplied endpoint limits allow 1024 output tokens. The 13 November complete run scored 80/80 with zero truncated calls and all categories passing. The gold JSONL and SHA-256 did not change.
why_others_rejected: Using an old but dated local catalog is acceptable for a reproducible demo but does not imply it reflects current CISA status; production freshness policy needs a separately reviewed setting. Increasing output allowance cannot make schema-valid or grounded content trustworthy by itself.
evidence_metric: 80/80; 232 Qwen calls; 0 truncations; 66 partial 11 completed 1 refused 2 validation; investigated P95 14.655 seconds; 152 offline tests passed
code_file: app/evidence.py; app/qwen.py; app/planner.py; app/analyst.py; app/critic.py; app/grading.py
risks_limitations: Single sequential demo run only; repeated-day evidence human gold review trace retention operations and concurrency remain unmeasured.

options_considered: Keep a separate Planner; combine its retrieval handoff into Evidence; compare one synthesis call with synthesis plus Critic using the same evidence
chosen: Remove Planner and InvestigationPlan; retain deterministic safety policy before the workflow; Evidence with Qwen interprets CVE/follow-up, queries and reviews RAG with one refined retry; run both architectures on identical frozen questions and grader
why_chosen: Planner had no distinct planning action beyond forwarding CVE information to retrieval. Same-gold evidence lets the added Critic responsibility be measured directly.
why_others_rejected: Not recorded - this row was written with one field missing; on 2026-11-17 the values from why_others_rejected onwards were shifted back into their own columns and the lost text was not reconstructed.
evidence_metric: Single-agent 80/80 in 300 calls, zero truncations, P95 15.368 s; multi-agent 80/80 in 377 calls, zero truncations, P95 16.188 s; evidence claims and retrieved passage IDs/text match for 77 evidence-bearing investigations; KEV source-name rubric regression passes CS-058 with no gold edits.
risks_limitations: Single run per architecture; Critic added 77 calls but did not change score; retrieval relevance for CS-058 remains a quality signal; fresh-CVE repeated-day human gold review trace-retention and concurrency evidence remain outstanding.

decision: Should the pages the NVD record itself cites be retrieval sources, and with what priority?
options_considered: Ignore reference links; merge fetched reference pages into the generic chunk index; keep a separate reference store searched first for the investigated CVE
chosen: Separate store (data/processed/reference_chunks.jsonl) with per-CVE tags; Evidence agent searches the investigated CVE's own references first and places those citations ahead of generic hybrid BM25+dense+RRF results
why_chosen: NVD cites these pages as the authoritative references for the CVE and vendor advisories do not exist in the generic corpus; chunk rows carry the citing CVE ids so lookup is scoped; NVD_REF evidence uses validation_status retrieved and the generic chunks/index stay untouched so frozen retrieval benchmarks remain reproducible
why_others_rejected: Ignoring links left authoritative vendor guidance unused; merging into chunks.jsonl would force an index rebuild, break R0-R3 comparability and give no CVE-specific priority; rank_bm25 BM25Okapi idf collapses on tiny per-CVE sets (a term in half the docs scores idf 0) so the reference scorer uses Lucene-style smoothed idf log(1+(N-df+0.5)/(df+0.5)) which stays positive
evidence_metric: 365 of 526 unique reference URLs fetched (43.7 MB); 315 docs produced 3,341 chunks covering 34 of 56 referenced CVEs; Log4Shell smoke run ranked the oss-security post and Apache security page ahead of generic corpus; 159 offline tests passed
risks_limitations: 161 URLs failed permanently (403 bot walls incl. CISA, 425, 404, dead hosts); 22 referenced CVEs have no usable chunks (mostly 2026 CVEs whose vendor pages blocked fetching) and fall back to the generic corpus; reference pages are snapshot copies that may have changed since fetch and carry no fetch timestamp because the downloader did not record one

decision: How many RAG search rounds may the Evidence agent use when the reviewer judges results insufficient?
options_considered: Keep one retry; allow up to 3 generic RAG calls with reviewer-gated refinements; open agentic loop until sufficient
chosen: Up to 3 generic RAG calls per investigation: the initial query plus at most two reviewer-driven refinements, with already-used refined queries skipped and an explicit limitation recorded when all rounds exhaust while the reviewer still judges results insufficient
why_chosen: The user asked for up to 3 RAG calls because a first query built from limited user keywords may miss; the existing review-and-refine mechanism already made the retry decision from retrieved context, so raising the cap reuses the same gating. One Qwen review call per round bounds model spend and keeps the latency budget measurable.
why_others_rejected: An open loop until sufficient has unbounded latency and model cost; keeping one retry leaves known-bad retrieval unaddressed in 69 of 80 measured investigations where the reviewer wanted a second query.
evidence_metric: Unit tests: 3-round cap, repeated-refined-query stop, exhaustion limitation note (162 tests pass). Live CS-001 rerun finished in 14.953 s with 4 model calls and no retry needed because reference-first passages satisfied the reviewer on round 1; earlier 80-question run showed the retry firing 69/80 under the old cap.
risks_limitations: Worst case now reaches 6 Qwen calls (interpretation, 3 reviews, analyst, critic) and longer latency; real-model behavior rarely uses all 3 rounds; frozen 80-question results pre-date this change so cross-version comparisons need the version note.

decision: What should happen when the Critic finds the Analyst draft deficient?
options_considered: Report-only Critic (status quo); Critic sends the draft back for one bounded revision; open revise loop until the Critic passes
chosen: One bounded revision: a failing first review re-prompts the Analyst with the previous draft and the Critic's issues (CRITIC_REVISION_REQUEST), the Critic re-reviews the revised draft, and the workflow then proceeds to validation regardless of outcome; a revision that fails deterministic validation uses the existing deterministic fallback, and a failed post-revision review reverts to the original draft plus the first review with revision_review_failed recorded
why_chosen: Before this change Critic findings only became report limitations and the Analyst never saw them, so fixable problems (missing citations, thin sections) were never acted on; the user asked for the Analyst to be notified with feedback. The cap of one revision bounds model spend; reverting to the original draft when the re-review fails keeps the shipped draft and its review consistent, because first-review findings no longer describe a revised draft.
why_others_rejected: An open revise loop has unbounded latency and can loop on a critic that never passes; letting a failed second review kill the investigation discards a valid revised draft (observed live on CS-030 as CriticError 'Qwen did not return a valid Critic review' and report failed); shipping a revised draft under the first review's findings would attach stale findings to a draft they do not describe.
evidence_metric: 165 offline tests pass (revise-then-pass, cap-at-one, revision-output fallback, second-review-failure revert). Live CS-030 rerun: interpretation + 2 retrieval reviews + analyst + critic + revision analyst + critic = 7 Qwen calls, 28.7 s, deterministic grade 1.0, report honestly partial; a prior CS-030 attempt without the revert path failed the whole investigation when the second review was unparseable.
risks_limitations: Worst case 7 Qwen calls and 28.7-31.9 s observed, above the 20 s P95 target for affected cases; the Analyst sometimes re-fails deterministic validation on revision, falling back to deterministic text; revision only fires when the first review fails a status (8 of 80 in the 2026-11-16 multi run had Critic findings), so most investigations are unchanged; frozen 80-question results pre-date this change.

decision: What happens to a first Analyst draft that parses but breaks a deterministic content rule?
options_considered: Instant deterministic fallback (status quo); send the parsed draft to the Critic and the revision loop, deterministic fallback only as a last resort
chosen: Defer the fallback: a parsed-but-invalid first draft is kept and returned with draft_invalid; the Critic reviews it, the workflow forces revision even when the Critic passes (feeding the validation error as the issue), and deterministic assembly happens only for unparseable output or when the revision still fails
why_chosen: The user challenged the instant swap: a draft the model actually wrote should first be judged by the Critic and corrected through the revision loop before deterministic text replaces it. Keeping the invalid draft also means the Critic's semantic review now covers the invalid-draft path, not just the happy path.
why_others_rejected: Replacing the draft before review hides the failure from the Critic and discards fixable content. Shipping an invalid draft straight to validation would fail the whole report (the Final Validator re-runs validate_draft and raises), so the forced revision guarantees only valid drafts reach the validator. Unparseable output cannot be reviewed at all, so its immediate fallback stays.
evidence_metric: 169 offline tests pass (forced revision when the Critic passes, revert-to-fallback when the pre-revision draft was itself invalid, revision-output fallback, parsed-invalid-kept unit tests). Live CS-001 smoke: the real model's first draft parsed but broke a rule (first_draft_invalid true), the Critic reviewed it, revision ran and re-failed validation, deterministic fallback shipped, deterministic grade 1.0, status partial, 25.3 s total.
risks_limitations: An invalid first draft now costs up to 2 extra Qwen calls (review + revision) before fallback; if the first review itself errors on an invalid draft the investigation still fails (critic-node failure semantics unchanged); the trace records first_draft_invalid so fallback-after-revision stays visible; frozen 80-question results pre-date this change.

decision: Why did Critic-driven revision keep failing on live traffic, and can a prompt change fix it?

Separately, the revision prompt had never included the evidence package the task text referenced, leaving the model to rewrite citations blind; CS-030 revised successfully on its first attempt once the package was added.
why_others_rejected: Accepting the fallback would keep hiding a systematic, fixable model failure behind deterministic text; fixing only the revision prompt would leave the first pass broken (draft_invalid on nearly every CS-001 attempt); loosening validation to ignore unknown IDs would weaken the hallucinated-citation guard for a fixable prompt problem.
evidence_metric: 170 offline tests pass. decision: Why does the dense layer now search a FAISS index file instead of a NumPy matrix, and how was the shipped ranking rule kept intact through that switch?
options_considered: Keep the NumPy matrix; adopt FAISS and accept its raw order, re-benchmarking everything; adopt FAISS with an approximate index (IVF/HNSW) or scalar quantisation for speed; adopt FAISS exact IndexFlatIP but widen the candidate pool and settle the order deterministically; move the vectors into a vector-database service such as Qdrant or Chroma.
chosen: FAISS IndexFlatIP over data/index/embeddings.faiss, asked for k + 32 candidates, those candidates rescored in float64 and sorted by (score desc, row asc).
why_chosen: The project's only defensible comparison basis is that every frozen retrieval number was measured with one tie rule, so the backend has to reproduce it. IndexFlatIP is exact search: inner product on L2-normalised vectors is cosine, no recall is traded away, and the only remaining variable is ordering, which the widened candidate pool and float64 rescoring pin down. FAISS then owns the vector bytes as one file, so a serving process loads an index rather than holding a second copy of the matrix, and the same file can be swapped for an approximate index later without touching callers.
why_others_rejected: Keeping NumPy works but leaves the vectors as a raw array with no standard format and no headroom as the corpus grows. Raw FAISS order was measured, not assumed: 4 of 140 frozen queries and 59 of 2,000 stress queries reordered at k=50, and top-50 membership changed on 1 and 13 of them, because a heap pop order and SIMD accumulation differ from BLAS; that would have quietly invalidated every recorded recall and nDCG number. An approximate or quantised index changes which documents are in the pool at all, which is a retrieval-quality decision dressed up as an infrastructure one. A vector-database service adds a network hop and a second store to keep in sync, and the whole project runs with no data leaving this machine. 10,457 vectors is not a scale problem: dense latency was already ~8 ms and measured 8.1 ms after the switch, so no speedup was claimed.
evidence_metric: store-path ranking mismatches vs the NumPy rule: 0 of 140 frozen queries and 0 of 2,000 stress queries at k=8 and k=50 (raw FAISS: 4 and 59 at k=50); 60-query benchmark score fields identical to the 2026-11-06 artifact, per category included; index hashes for chunks, bm25 tokens, embeddings.npy and ids.json unchanged; 304 offline tests pass (13 new).
risks_limitations: CANDIDATE_MARGIN is a fixed 32, chosen because the corpus has 32 exact duplicate rows and a largest duplicate group of 19, so a query with more than 32 equal scores straddling the cut could still be ordered differently from the NumPy rule. The parity check is a sample (every 5th indexed vector capped at 2,000) over the 140 distinct strings in the three evaluation files, not an exhaustive proof, and it reads embeddings.npy, so dropping that file would degrade the guarantee to the unit tests alone. embeddings.npy is kept as that comparison seed, not as a live backend, so the index directory now carries the vectors twice (~32 MB). BM25, RRF fusion and the reference-first retriever were untouched, so only the dense layer's provenance moved.

category: Evaluation validity / per-claim RAG and LLM metrics on a live re-run
decision: Why could the Batch 10 evaluation columns not stay answer-level, and what makes a per-claim LLM measure worth printing?
options_considered: Keep the answer-level columns and only document that they repeat; add per-claim ROUGE and cosine only; add a free-form per-claim LLM judge; add a per-claim judge that only locates and quotes required elements while code computes the score.
chosen: Two layers written beside the 17 November columns in new columns BP-BY, never over them. Deterministic per-claim RAG measures (which retrieved item answers this claim, evidence support grade, support ratio, anchor coverage and grade, citation precision, per-claim ROUGE-1/2/L over the section-scoped answer text the claim was graded on, per-claim MiniLM cosine) plus a per-claim LLM judge b10-claim-1.1 that returns one status and one verbatim quote per required element, with score_elements() computing agreement and verdict in code: a stated or contradicted element whose quote is not literally in the answer is downgraded to unquoted, so inventing a quote cannot raise a row. Both judge caches now key on the answer's SHA-256 as well as the dataset hash and prompt version. The numbers come from a new live end-to-end run of all 10 investigations on the FAISS backend, one active Qwen request at a time.
why_chosen: A gold claim is one row, so its evaluation must be one number per row; the deterministic layer already varied per claim and only the descriptive and LLM layers were flat. Keying the cache on the answer hash is what makes a re-run honest: with the dataset hash alone, a new trace directory silently reuses the previous run's verdicts, which is exactly the constant-value symptom the user spotted.
why_others_rejected: Answer-level ROUGE, cosine and judge grades a whole report; repeated on 11 rows it is correct arithmetic but reads as a stub. A free-form per-claim judge was tried and thrown away, not tuned.
evidence_metric: Live run: 10 of 10 investigations HTTP 200 (7 completed, 3 partial), mean 19.887 s and median 21.072 s per investigation (11.69-24.208), 5.5 model calls and 17,327 tokens mean, 173,272 tokens total. Deterministic field check clean on 10 of 10 investigations; per-claim verdicts Pass 53 / Partial 21 / Fail 26 / Abstain 10, and 109 of 110 verdicts identical to the 17 November run with one Fail -> Pass. Per-claim measures now differ row by row: claim_rougeL 0.0000-0.9545, claim_cosine 0.1061-0.9000, and in the workbook columns BP-BY the per-claim judge column is distinct on 110 of 110 rows (per-claim ROUGE 83, per-claim cosine 105, per-claim support 86) while the two answer-level columns show the 10 values they are labelled as having. Claim judge over 110 claims: conveys 58, partial 34, contradicts 12, misses 6, agreement mean 4.0273 (range 1-5), element share mean 0.7758, 219 stated / 40 unquotable / 26 missing / 15 contradicted / 2 conceded elements, judge errors 0. Answer-level judge mean factual 4.2, completeness 4.2, groundedness 4.2, overall 4.1, strict pass 7 of 10. Concordance of the per-claim judge with the deterministic audit: 'conveys' matches a Pass or Abstain on 59 of 110 rows, reported as a crosstab rather than as a score. 336 offline tests pass (32 new).
