category: Presentation of frozen evaluation data / read-only dashboards for report writing
decision: How do the evaluation columns that live in the two frozen workbooks get shown well enough to write a 12-page capstone report, without the viewer ever inventing, recomputing or re-typing a number?
options_considered: A separate static HTML report; a tab inside the existing investigation page; one new Streamlit page per view over both frozen sets; a viewer that recomputes the metrics from the traces so the numbers look fresh; a viewer that only reads the stored artifacts and prints 'not captured' for anything absent.
chosen: Two new Streamlit pages (pages/1_Evaluation_RAG.py, pages/2_Evaluation_LLM.py) on one read-only layer, app/eval_dashboard.py, that computes nothing: workbook text joined by test_id/claim_id to the numbers already stored in metrics.csv, retrieval.csv and batch10 scores.json, retrieved passages and the full answer text read from the run traces, one radio over both frozen sets, and CSV plus paste-ready Markdown export per table and per CVE.
why_chosen: The report needs figures a person can trust and copy, so the risk is not ugliness but silent fabrication. Reading only the artifacts that produced the published verdicts means every cell on screen has a file behind it, and every detail view prints those paths. An empty cell says 'not captured' instead of showing a plausible zero, which is how the earlier judge column was found to be unmarked. The Batch 10 answer is rendered from the trace report rather than the workbook because both the workbook copy and generated_claim are capped at 1,200 characters while real answers reach 2,444, so the capped copy would have displayed a text nobody graded. Export is part of the design: re-typing a table into a report is where a 0.3704 becomes a 0.3740.
why_others_rejected: A static HTML file duplicates the app and goes stale the moment an artifact is re-run. A tab inside the investigation page buries evaluation data under the operational sidebar and cannot carry 110 claim rows. Recomputing metrics in the viewer would create a second, slightly different measurement of the same run - the exact failure mode D30 had to document for answer-level versus per-claim granularity. A viewer that left blanks silent would repeat the 'dummy value' complaint the user had already raised once.
evidence_metric: 369 offline tests pass in 24.45 s, 33 in tests/test_eval_dashboard.py (29 data-layer + 4 new AppTest page-render tests). 9 headless widget-state runs across both pages, both datasets and filter/selectbox states returned no exception and no st.error. On screen the frozen numbers reproduce: golden deterministic verdict PASS on 100 of 100 rows, Batch 10 per-claim Pass 53 / Partial 21 / Fail 26 / Abstain 10, 110 claim rows over 10 investigations, one Markdown export of 23,166 characters for CS-B10-01. First browser render failed with TypeError: CodeMixin.code() got an unexpected keyword argument 'wrap' (Streamlit 1.67 calls it wrap_lines) while all 29 data-layer tests stayed green - the reason the page-render tests exist.
output_artifact: Two dashboard routes on the Streamlit app: /Evaluation_RAG and /Evaluation_LLM, each with an all-rows table, a filter, a one-CVE detail view and CSV/Markdown exports; 1,401 new lines across the layer, the two pages and their tests.
risks_limitations: The viewer is only as current as the artifacts: a new run needs the writer scripts to have run first, or the page prints 'not captured'. Recall and precision on the RAG page are rules-only proxies measured against the gold answer's own terms, never model judgements, and the deterministic source-derived field check stays the only pass/fail authority. A Streamlit process started before pages/ existed does not list the new routes, so the UI must be restarted to see them. Nothing leaves the machine: the pages read local files only and make no network call.

category: Embedding / hosted endpoint replaces the local model
decision: Why did every vector in the system move from a local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model to the course's hosted bge-small-en-v1.5 endpoint, and what did the endpoint's token ceiling force into the design?
options_considered: Keep the local MiniLM model; use the endpoint only for retrieval and keep the local model for the similarity metric; use the endpoint for both jobs; send the whole chunk and let the server truncate; cut every chunk to a single globally safe character budget; cut with a character budget and re-cut only what the server rejects.
chosen: The endpoint for both jobs: dense retrieval vectors (index build and query embedding) and the descriptive answer-vs-reference cosine, with 2,200-character pre-cut plus an exact re-cut driven by the token count the server reports.
why_chosen: The user directed it, and one model defining every vector removes the failure mode where queries and stored vectors live in different spaces. The endpoint is course-operated and reached over verified TLS with the repository's own CA file, so it does not add a third party. MiniLM and bge-small are both 384-dimensional BERT-family models, so the index shape, the FAISS backend and the rescoring rule all stayed.
why_others_rejected: Retrieval only, or the metric only, would leave two embedding models in one evaluation and two vector spaces to keep straight. Server-side truncation does not exist here: an over-long input is rejected with HTTP 422, so trusting it would fail the request, not shorten the text. A single globally safe 1,816-character cap would encode only 86.09% of corpus characters, less than the MiniLM index carried, while the measured re-cut keeps 93.79%.
evidence_metric: Measured against the endpoint: 384 dims, norms already 1.00000, identical text 1.0000 vs unrelated 0.3665; density 0.1999 tokens/char prose, 0.2659 dense, 0.2813 table-heavy; ceiling enforced per input (a 16-text batch of 502 prompt_tokens accepted, a single 519-token input rejected). Calibration on 512 strided chunks: 362 requests, 145 pre-cuts, 58 re-cuts, 51.2 s (about 100 ms per chunk).
code_file: app/embeddings.py::EmbeddingsClient; app/retrieval.py::Retriever.embedder; app/answer_layers.py::cosine; scripts/build_index.py (no --model flag on purpose)
output_artifact: data/index/embeddings.faiss + data/manifests/index.json (model bge-small-en-v1.5, dim 384); vm02-ca.crt; tests/test_embeddings.py (13 offline tests)
risks_limitations: The vectors are no longer reproducible offline: a fresh checkout re-embeds 10,457 chunks against a live endpoint, so an outage blocks index rebuild, and the served model weights cannot be inspected. A cosine before the swap is not comparable with one after, so the two are never mixed in a column or table. The superseded MiniLM index survives only as a quarantined copy.

category: Fresh-checkout reproducibility / the NVD cache ships and the live Batch 10 columns were re-measured on the hosted index
decision: Why did the Batch 10 workbook's live evaluation columns get rewritten, and what did materialising a fresh checkout of the tree expose about which files the runtime actually needs?
options_considered: Keep quoting the 17 November run as the shipped system's numbers; re-run the 10 investigations on the rebuilt bge-small index and overwrite columns 68-77; keep all of data/raw ignored and make the first run call scripts/snapshot_nvd.py; ship only the 10 CVE records Batch 10 needs; ship the whole 155-record NVD cache.
chosen: Re-run and overwrite, which is what the user chose: the 10 investigations ran again against the index that ships and columns 68-77 carry that run, with the MiniLM-era live run quarantined rather than deleted. data/processed (71 MB corpus) and data/raw/nvd (155 records, 2.26 MB) ship; data/index (53 MB) and the rest of data/raw stay ignored and are rebuilt or re-fetched by command.
why_chosen: The user's requirement was that a git checkout on a new PC runs end to end. A number under a header naming bge-small has to have come from the bge-small index, and the frozen corpus has to be present for chunks_sha256 and every recorded number to reproduce. The NVD cache is not optional bulk: app/evidence.py reads data/raw/nvd/<CVE>.json for the CVSS vector and the affected-product facts, so a checkout without it cannot answer the frozen questions at all.
why_others_rejected: Leaving the 17 November block labelled current would put answers produced by MiniLM retrieval under headers naming the new model, and the 17 November answers cannot be regenerated because the model that retrieved them is retired. Deleting the superseded run would destroy the only MiniLM/bge-small comparison, and with no commit in this repository there is nothing to undo a delete with. Requiring a live NVD fetch before the first run would make the frozen facts depend on a source that changes. Shipping only the 10 Batch 10 CVEs would leave the cached records the earlier sets' traces cite out of the tree.
evidence_metric: Fresh-checkout proof on 2026-11-18 in a scratch directory holding a copy of the git ls-files -o --exclude-standard list: main has no commit, so copying that list stands in for the checkout, and what is proven is the sufficiency of the file set rather than the git mechanics. Stage 1, the list printed 134 files when the copy was taken at 14:32: 338 offline tests pass with no data/index present, and scripts.build_index re-embedded the corpus there - 10,457 chunks in 15 m 04 s (4,847 requests, ~3.36 M model tokens) producing embeddings.faiss, embeddings.npy and ids.json with SHA-256 identical to the shipped index, only the manifest generated_at differing - which is sound because only data/processed feeds the index. D33 run as written to the workbook: 10/10 HTTP 200, 8 completed / 2 partial, mean 23.973 s, claim verdicts Pass 52 / Partial 22 / Fail 26 / Abstain 10, 109 of 110 verdicts identical to the 17 November run with one Fail to Partial, answer-level field check clean on 10/10. category: History provenance / every history row names the index it retrieved with
decision: Why did the Streamlit History tab still list 16 investigations from before the embedding swap as if they were current, and what does a row record now?
options_considered: Leave the journal in place and accept the mixed list; delete it; move it out of the tree and stamp every new row with the index it used; re-investigate the 16 questions so every row is stamped
chosen: Archive plus stamp, which is what the user chose. data/traces/investigations.jsonl (16 rows, 586,297 bytes, sha256 80df3cd1eed435641d5144670e9630c4cf7a30b4774d75fb98d88776e2eeb06f) was moved to the quarantine folder with a MANIFEST.md section, nothing deleted. app/history.py now writes a runtime block into every record - embeddings_model, embeddings_dim, dense_backend, chunks_sha256 and index_generated_at read once from data/manifests/index.json, falling back to the configured model when that file is absent - and HistoryEntry carries embeddings_model and index_chunks_sha256 as optional fields so pre-stamp rows still parse. The History tab adds a Vectors column, bge-small-en-v1.5 . 72a0ce2e, and says not recorded where a row predates the stamp.
why_chosen: The complaint was that stale rows looked current. Nothing in the 16 old records names an embedding model, and 2 of them carry retrieval_meta of null, so none of them can be attributed to an index; a row that cannot name its vectors is indistinguishable from one the retired MiniLM index produced. Stamping at write time puts the fact where it belongs, in the system of record, and the read path only reports it.
why_others_rejected: Deleting the journal would be unrecoverable because main still has no commit. Leaving the rows in place keeps the misreporting. Re-investigating the 16 questions would spend 16 live Qwen workflows to rewrite answers that are already archived, and would still not reproduce what the retired index retrieved.
evidence_metric: 343 offline tests pass (338 before this change plus 5 new). Live check through the restarted service: POST /investigate returned HTTP 200 / completed in 26,728 ms, the stored record carries runtime {embeddings_model bge-small-en-v1.5, embeddings_dim 384, dense_backend faiss.IndexFlatIP, chunks_sha256 72a0ce2e829fc64faee7092e1b06b0b7320363f15fa07d5d7367e36acdbb5919, index_generated_at 2026-11-18T08:35:05+00:00}, GET /history exposes embeddings_model and index_chunks_sha256, and the History tab rendered exactly one row with Vectors bge-small-en-v1.5 . 72a0ce2e instead of the 16 unstamped ones.
